The '''National Cyber Security Centre''' ('''NCSC''', Irish: ''An Lárionad Náisiúnta Cibearshlándála'') is a government [[computer security]] organisation in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], an operational arm of the [[Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration]]. The NCSC was developed in 2013 and formally established by the [[Government of Ireland|Irish government]] in July 2015. It is responsible for Ireland's cyber security, with a primary focus on securing government networks, protecting [[Critical infrastructure|critical national infrastructure]], and assisting businesses and citizens in protecting their own systems.<ref name="cyber 1">{{cite web|title=National Cyber Security Strategy 2015-2017|url=http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/NR/rdonlyres/80C30B53-336F-45EF-9BDE-63F02A0E88C4/0/NationalCyberSecurityStrategy20152017.pdf|publisher=Department of Communications, Energy and Natural Resources|accessdate=7 July 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714150335/http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/NR/rdonlyres/80C30B53-336F-45EF-9BDE-63F02A0E88C4/0/NationalCyberSecurityStrategy20152017.pdf|archivedate=14 July 2015}}</ref> The NCSC incorporates the Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT-IE).

The NCSC is headquartered at  Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration, 51 [[St Stephen's Green]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Cyber Security Centre - Contact page |url=https://www.ncsc.gov.ie/contact/ |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=National Cyber Security Centre}}</ref>

==Mandate and organisation==
The mandate for the NCSC includes; 
* activities to reduce the vulnerability of critical systems and networks within the state to incidents and [[cyber-attack]]s;
* effective response when such attacks occur;
* responsibility for the [[Critical infrastructure protection|protection of critical information infrastructure]];
* establishing and maintaining cooperative relationships with national and international partners.<ref name="cyber 1"/>

Threats identified to Ireland's critical infrastructure and government networks include: lone individuals, activist groups, criminal groups, terrorist groups, and nation states seeking to gather intelligence or to damage or degrade infrastructure. Incidents arising through extreme weather, human error and hardware or software failure also pose significant risks to individuals, businesses and public administration.<ref name="cyber 1"/><ref>{{cite news|last1=Cullen|first1=Adam|title=Cyber-crime gangs with global threat detected within Ireland|url=http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/news/cybercrime-gangs-with-global-threat-detected-within-ireland-31093475.html|accessdate=8 July 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|date=25 March 2015}}</ref>

Work relating to the National Cyber Security Centre, and any records associated with the security of [[Information and communications technology|ICT]] systems in the state and outside it, are exempt from being disclosed under [[Freedom of information laws by country#Ireland|freedom of information]] (FOI).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wall|first1=Martin|last2=Duncan|first2=Pamela|title=State 'vulnerable' to cyber attacks if security documents exposed, official said|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/news/technology/state-vulnerable-to-cyber-attacks-if-security-documents-exposed-official-said-1.1718469|accessdate=8 July 2015|publisher=The Irish Times|date=10 March 2014}}</ref>

Richard Browne was appointed as the NCSC's director in January 2022, having served as acting director for the previous 18 months.<ref name=new-director-appointed-Jan2022/>

===Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT-IE)===
The '''Computer Security Incident Response Team''' ('''CSIRT-IE''') was established in late 2011 (prior to the official formation of the NCSC) within the Department of Communications, Energy and Natural Resources, and includes secondees from other government agencies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cybercrime Network Conference (CyNC) 2013, Closing speech by Alan Shatter TD Minister for Justice, Equality and Defence|url=http://www.justice.ie/en/JELR/Pages/SP13000417|publisher=Dept of Justice and Equality|accessdate=8 July 2015}}</ref> The main role of CSIRT-IE is to provide a 24/7 expert [[Computer emergency response team|emergency response to computer security incidents]] across all public sector bodies, as well as to provide advice to reduce threat exposure. CSIRT-IE engages in emergency planning with government agencies overseen by the [[Office of Emergency Planning (Ireland)|Office of Emergency Planning]] (OEP) within the [[Department of Defence (Ireland)|Department of Defence]] and the [[Office of Emergency Planning (Ireland)#Government Task Force on Emergency Planning|Government Task Force on Emergency Planning]], chaired by the [[Minister for Defence (Ireland)|Minister for Defence]]. CSIRT-IE shares information with the [[European Network and Information Security Agency|European Union Agency for Network and Information Security]] (ENISA).<ref>{{cite news|title=National Cyber Security Strategy published|url=http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/Press+Releases/2015/National+Cyber+Security+Strategy+published.htm|accessdate=7 July 2015|publisher=DCENR|date=2 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708144936/http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/Press+Releases/2015/National+Cyber+Security+Strategy+published.htm|archive-date=8 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Outlining the future core aspects of the work of the NCSC, the government's ''[https://web.archive.org/web/20150714150335/http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/NR/rdonlyres/80C30B53-336F-45EF-9BDE-63F02A0E88C4/0/NationalCyberSecurityStrategy20152017.pdf National Cyber Security Strategy 2015-2017]'' states that the NCSC is to seek formal international accreditation for a Government CSIRT (g/CSIRT), expected in 2016, and accreditation will be sought for a formal National CSIRT (n/CSIRT), while also developing a capacity in the area of [[Industrial control system|Industrial Control Systems]] and [[SCADA]], which are used to run vital state networks such as electricity, water and telecommunications.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kennedy|first1=John|title=Ireland gears up for cyber war – new strategy to protect critical infrastructure|url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/enterprise/2015/07/03/ireland-gears-up-for-cyber-war-new-strategy-to-protect-critical-infrastructure|accessdate=8 July 2015|publisher=Silicon Republic|date=3 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=National Cyber Security Strategy 2015-2017|url=http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/Communications/Business+and+Technology/Cyber+Security/National+Cyber+Security.htm|publisher=Department of Communications, Energy and Natural Resources Ireland|accessdate=7 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705234712/http://www.dcenr.gov.ie/Communications/Business+and+Technology/Cyber+Security/National+Cyber+Security.htm|archive-date=5 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Inter-departmental cooperation==
[[File:Cis intel curragh offices,co.kildare.PNG|thumbnail|The Defence Forces [[Communications & Information Services Corps|CIS Corps]] work closely with the NCSC]]
There is a strong culture of cooperation between the National Cyber Security Centre and the [[Defence Forces (Ireland)|Irish Defence Forces]] in areas regarding technical skill sets, technical information sharing and exercise participation. Arrangements are due to be formalised by means of a [[Service-level agreement|Service Level Agreement]] with the Department of Defence, including a mechanism for the immediate sharing of technical expertise and information in the event of a major national cyber incident or emergency. The branch of the Irish military with responsibility for cyber defence is the [[Communications & Information Services Corps|Communications and Information Services Corps]] (CIS).<ref>{{cite news|title=Military 'can help stop cyber attacks'|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/military-can-help-stop-cyber-attacks-313573.html|accessdate=8 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 February 2015}}</ref>

The [[Garda Síochána]], the national police service, is involved with the NCSC in a preventative and investigative capacity, with regard to [[national security]] and [[computer crime]]. Its liaison relationships with international security services are particularly helpful to the NCSC in identifying emerging threats and vulnerabilities, and establishing best practice preventative measures. There is to be a Memorandum of Understanding with the [[Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration]] on this matter, and upcoming cyber legislation will support the work of the National Cyber Security Centre.<ref name="cyber 1"/>

There is also a [[Memorandum of understanding|Memorandum of Understanding]] with the [[Centre for Cybersecurity & Cybercrime Investigation]] (CCI) at [[University College Dublin]], Europe's leading centre for research and education in cybersecurity, cybercrime and [[digital forensics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Centre for Cybersecurity & Cybercrime Investigation, University College Dublin|url=http://www.ucd.ie/cci/|publisher=UCD|accessdate=8 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Gordon|title=Cyber security a safe bet for growth|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/business/technology/cyber-security-a-safe-bet-for-growth-1.1279774|accessdate=8 July 2015|publisher=The Irish Times|date=28 January 2011}}</ref>

==International cooperation==
In 2024 the NCSC took part in [[Locked Shields]] jointly with a team from [[South Korea]], run by [[Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence]].<ref name=rte-cybersecurity-exercise-could-be-for-real-tomorrow>{{Cite news |title=Cybersecurity exercise could be 'for real tomorrow' - NCSC |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2024/0425/1445627-cyber-security/ |last=O'Donovan |first=Brian |date=2024-05-03 |access-date=2024-05-08 |publisher=[[RTÉ News]]}}</ref><ref name=it-ireland-takes-part-in-nato-cyber-wargame>{{Cite news |title=Ireland takes part in Nato cyber wargame, testing defence from hackers and bots |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/2024/04/25/ireland-takes-part-in-nato-cyber-wargame-testing-defence-from-hackers-and-bots/ |last=Gallagher |first=Conor |date=2024-04-25 |access-date=2024-05-08 |work=[[Irish Times]]}}</ref> The Irish team played the part of a cybersecurity team for the fictional state of Berylia, which was attacked by hackers from the fictional state of Crimsonia.<ref name=rte-cybersecurity-exercise-could-be-for-real-tomorrow/><ref name=it-ireland-takes-part-in-nato-cyber-wargame/> Ireland joined CCDCOE in 2023 and took part for the first time in Locked Shields in 2024.<ref name=rte-cybersecurity-exercise-could-be-for-real-tomorrow/><ref name=it-ireland-takes-part-in-nato-cyber-wargame/> Richard Browne said of the simulated attack "It’s like the 2021 incident but with very sophisticated actors at the other end, not just petty criminals like the HSE attack".<ref name=it-ireland-takes-part-in-nato-cyber-wargame/>
